subject: Post-demo: model-fit qualification and parity follow-up
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@ledgerly.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Nair <rajiv@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks — post-demo asks on parity + benchmark materials

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo today — the team found the latency and conversational routing compelling. A few asks we discussed internally and want to confirm next steps on: 

- Parity: we need a short write-up comparing an open-model candidate to our in-house baseline (Ledgerly Core v3). Specifically, can you surface: precision/recall benchmarks on our key intents, hallucination counts on the same prompt set, and token-level cost estimates?
- Acceptance thresholds: our product team is leaning toward minimum F1 0.88 for classification/intents and <1.5% hallucination on knowledge-base QA. Any thoughts on realistic thresholds for open candidates?
- Prompt sets: can you share the prompt bundle (sample prompts + expected outputs) you used in the demo and the evaluation harness so we can run local checks?
- Regressions: we need a plan to detect/alert on quality regressions post-rollout (prompt drift, distribution shifts).

Attached is our RFP excerpt to help prioritize metrics. Can you share an internal plan and shortlist of open models you recommend for a 2-week trial?

Thanks,
Anna

--
Anna Keller
Head of Product — Ledgerly
anna.keller@ledgerly.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Ledgerly_RFP_2027.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Rajiv Nair <rajiv@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — post-demo asks on parity + benchmark materials

Hi Anna — great to meet you and the product team yesterday. Appreciate the RFP excerpt — that helps focus the metrics. Quick summary and proposed next steps: 

Summary of asks (I): parity evidence vs Ledgerly Core v3, (II) prompt bundle + evaluation harness, (III) regression/monitoring plan, (IV) a 2-week trial with defined acceptance gates.

Proposed immediate plan: 
- I will share the exact prompt bundle and our evaluation harness link (internal) — see items below.
- Recommended open-model shortlist for initial trials: OSS-Llama2-13B-instruct (lower-cost baseline), Falcon-40B-instruct (strong generative fidelity), Redwood-7B-quant (latency-cost friendly, tuned for instruction-following).
- Acceptance thresholds suggestion (initial): classification F1 >= 0.86 (we'll tune prompts), QA hallucination <= 1.0% on the KB test set, end-to-end p95 latency < 300ms on dedicated capacity. These are starting points — Marissa and Neha will run focused benchmarks and propose stricter gates if feasible.

If you're comfortable, we'd like to: (A) run a 2-week trial on a small sample of your traffic (sanitized) starting as soon as next Monday (6/14), and (B) prepare a parity one-pager comparing the open candidates against Core v3 on your prompt set.

I will also loop in Product (Marissa) and Applied ML (Neha) to execute the benchmarks and to produce the trial plan.

Best,
Vivek
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
leadership@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Thanks — post-demo asks on parity + benchmark materials

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Anna's RFP excerpt and the asks. High-level asks: parity summary vs their proprietary baseline, share prompt bundle + evaluation harness, run short trial and report acceptance metrics.

Please action:
- Marissa: build the one-page parity readout (comparison table + quick notes on operational tradeoffs).
- Neha: run the initial bench (3 open candidates below) on their prompt set and return metrics: precision/recall (per-intent), QA hallucination rate, latency p50/p95, and token cost estimate. Also produce the prompt_bundle_v1.zip we can share.
- Deliverables target: initial draft by EOD 6/11.

Open candidates to bench: OSS-Llama2-13B-instruct, Falcon-40B-instruct, Redwood-7B-quant. Note: we may include a quantized 13B variant if latency looks too high.

Attachments to produce for the external send: redwood_prompt_bundle_v1.zip, trial-plan-ledgerly.pdf. I'll copy you both on the outbound.

Thanks — Vivek
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Thanks — post-demo asks on parity + benchmark materials

Quick bench summary (initial run, dev harness on their sanitized prompt bundle):

Candidates tested:
- OSS-Llama2-13B-instruct (13B FP16)
- Falcon-40B-instruct (40B FP16)
- Redwood-7B-quant (7B int8 tuned)

Key metrics (aggregated across Ledgerly prompt set):
- Intent classification (macro avg F1): Llama2-13B: 0.84 | Falcon-40B: 0.87 | Redwood-7B-quant: 0.82
- KB QA hallucination rate (measured as hallucinations per 1k answers): Llama2-13B: 2.1% | Falcon-40B: 1.1% | Redwood-7B-quant: 0.9%
- Latency (p95, dedicated small-cap pool): Llama2-13B: 420ms | Falcon-40B: 510ms | Redwood-7B-quant: 210ms
- Token cost estimate (per 1M tokens, infra cost): Llama2-13B: $420 | Falcon-40B: $760 | Redwood-7B-quant: $180

Interpretation & recommendation:
- Parity vs Ledgerly Core v3: based on the initial metrics and Ledgerly's target F1 0.88, Falcon-40B is closest on F1 but costs and latency are less favorable. Redwood-7B-quant shows the best latency/cost profile and a low hallucination rate, but falls short on F1. Llama2-13B sits in the middle.
- Shortlist for the 2-week trial: Falcon-40B-instruct (accuracy-focused), Redwood-7B-quant (latency/cost-focused).
- Acceptance gates (proposal for trial):
  - Classification macro F1 >= 0.88 (or within 2 points of Core v3 if absolute parity not achievable in 2 weeks)
  - KB QA hallucination <= 1.2%
  - Production p95 latency <= 300ms on Dedicated pool
  - No more than 2% downstream regression in critical intent routing (monitored by their key metrics)

Monitoring / regression plan (outline):
- Live monitors: rolling 24h sample of QA responses to measure hallucination signal + smoke tests every deploy.
- Prompt-set drift detection: weekly similarity checks vs seed prompts; flag if n-gram overlap drops below threshold.
- Regression alerts: automated triage in Console with example traces and prompt/response diffs; severity routed to CS + Engineering.

Attached: prompt bundle (redwood_prompt_bundle_v1.zip) and a draft trial plan (trial-plan-ledgerly.pdf). Links to the internal bench notebook and parity template below.

Links: https://drive.redwood.com/marissa/benchmarks/ledgerly-parity-report
Notebook: https://notebooks.redwood.com/bench/ldg-2027-0421

Will iterate on the parity one-pager if you want different acceptance numbers.

—Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@ledgerly.com>, Rajiv Nair <rajiv@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

- Regression plan: automated drift detection, 24h hallucination monitoring, Console alert routing to your CS and our engineering team.

3) Sign the trial Terms (DocuSign link) — I'll send immediately after you confirm.

If that works I’ll start the trial provisioning with the infra team and schedule a 30-minute sync with Neha for runbook handoff.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
